When planning a home transformation, one of the first questions to settle is whether you need an interior decorator or an interior designer — and the answer matters more than most people realise. The two roles are frequently confused, yet they cover very different ground: one focuses purely on aesthetics, the other on structural planning and compliance. Understanding the interior decorator vs designer distinction upfront can save you time, money, and the frustration of hiring the wrong professional for your project.

By Mae Osz | Interior Design Consultant & Home Decor Expert with 12+ years of experience. 

Quick Answer: An interior decorator focuses on the look and feel of a space — selecting furniture, colour schemes, wall art, and accessories — without making structural changes. An interior designer has formal training in spatial planning, building regulations, and technical layouts, making them suited to more complex projects involving structural alterations. For most cosmetic home refreshes, a decorator is sufficient; for renovations or extensions, a designer is the right choice.

Have you ever found yourself wondering who exactly you need to hire to bring your dream home to life? Maybe you're thinking of a fresh look, or perhaps you want to make a space feel truly calming and stylish. Over my 12 years helping homeowners, I've heard countless questions about the interior decorator vs designer debate. It's a question that often causes confusion, yet understanding this can transform how smoothly your project runs and how beautiful your space ends up.

Choosing the right professional means you achieve the look you want without costly misunderstandings or wasted effort. I've seen homeowners make decisions based on assumptions that sometimes lead to frustration or half-finished projects. If you're curious about what sets these two apart, you're in the right place.

Wall art and interiors go hand in hand. Whether it's selecting the perfect piece or curating a space that feels calm and inviting, knowing the difference between an interior decorator vs designer helps guide the process naturally.

What Is the Difference Between an Interior Decorator vs Designer?

Many clients come to me with a simple question: "What's the real difference between an interior decorator vs designer?" It's an easy mix-up, but these two roles have distinct focuses. Getting this right from the start saves time, money, and the frustration of hiring someone whose skills don't match what your project actually needs.

Core Difference in Focus

An interior decorator enhances the aesthetic of a space — selecting colours, furniture, wall art, accessories, fabrics, and lighting to create an atmosphere that expresses your style. An interior designer takes a broader approach, planning the functionality and structure of interiors, often working on architectural changes, layouts, and building regulations compliance. The simplest way to remember it: a decorator makes a space look beautiful, whilst a designer makes it work differently.

Real-Life Example

Recently, I helped a couple in Manchester who wanted to refresh their living room. After discussing their needs, it was clear they only wanted to update furniture, choose calming wall art, and improve lighting without structural alterations — perfect for an interior decorator. Visit our home decor trends page for styling inspiration.

Training and Qualifications: How Do Decorators and Designers Compare?


Shop Here

One common mistake is assuming interior decorators do the same technical work as designers. In reality, their training varies greatly. This distinction matters because it directly affects what each professional is legally and practically able to do on your project — and what happens if something goes wrong.

Educational Background

  • Interior Designers usually have formal education in design disciplines — architecture, spatial planning, building codes, and materials science.
  • Interior Decorators learn through professional courses focusing on colour theory, furniture styles, fabrics, and aesthetics rather than structural elements.

Neither path is superior — they simply prepare professionals for different types of work. A highly skilled decorator with years of experience can transform a space just as dramatically as a designer, provided the project doesn't require structural input.

Services Offered: Which Professional Suits Your Project Needs?

Interior Decorators generally focus on furniture, accessories, and artwork selection, colour schemes and textiles, window treatments, and styling. Interior Designers offer space planning, structural changes, building regulations consultations, and project management with contractors. Understanding which services you actually need is the most important step before making any hiring decision — many homeowners pay for a designer when a decorator would have delivered exactly what they wanted at a fraction of the cost. Equally, some projects genuinely require a designer's technical expertise, and cutting corners there can create problems that are expensive to fix later.

Cost and Timeline: What to Expect with Decorators and Designers


Shop Here

Generally, interior decorators charge less because their scope is more focused and less technical. Interior designers, due to their specialised training and complexity of projects, often come with higher fees and longer timelines. It's worth getting detailed quotes from both before committing — some designers offer initial consultations at a fixed fee, which can help you understand whether their involvement is genuinely necessary for your project.

Service Type Typical Duration Key Factors
Interior Decoration 2 to 6 weeks Furniture delivery, art sourcing, styling
Interior Design 2 to 6 months Planning, permits, construction, installations

Choosing the Right Professional for Your Home Interior


Shop Here
  • Project Scope: If plans involve moving walls or updating kitchens, go for an interior designer.
  • Decor Refresh: For new furniture, accessories, and artwork, an interior decorator delivers impressive results.
  • Budget and Timeline: Designers may require a bigger budget and longer timeline.
  • Professional Chemistry: Meet a few professionals and assess how well they understand your tastes.

Don't underestimate that last point — the best professional for your project is the one who genuinely listens to what you want rather than imposing their own aesthetic. A good decorator or designer will ask as many questions as they answer in the first meeting.

Training, Experience & Project Scope: How Do Interior Decorators and Designers Differ?

Interior designers usually undergo several years of education, gaining skills in structural planning. Decorators focus more on aesthetics and finishing touches, specialising in elements like wall art placement and furniture styling. In practice, the most experienced decorators develop an intuitive understanding of space and proportion that rivals a designer's technical knowledge — the difference is that they can't legally sign off on structural work. When reviewing portfolios, look for projects that match your own ambitions in scale and style rather than simply choosing the most impressive-looking work.

How Do the Costs and Timelines of Hiring an Interior Decorator vs Designer Differ?

Decorators typically offer quicker turnarounds focused on styling, whilst designers may take longer due to the scale of work. Always check detailed quotes before starting and ensure expectations are aligned. A decorator refreshing a living room might complete the project in three to four weeks; a designer overseeing a full kitchen and dining room remodel could take four to six months from initial brief to final installation. Building in a contingency budget of 10–15% is sensible for either type of project.

Which Professional Is Best for Certain Home Decor Projects?


Shop Here

For repainting, new furniture, or adding beautiful wall art, a decorator is ideal. For major remodels, lighting rewiring, or spatial changes, a designer is the way to go. A useful rule of thumb: if the project requires a tradesperson — a plumber, electrician, or builder — you almost certainly need a designer to coordinate and oversee that work. If it only requires deliveries and styling decisions, a decorator will handle it beautifully.

How Can I Understand the General Differences So I Can Choose the Right Professional?


Shop Here

Think about what you want changed or enhanced. Ask yourself: "Am I looking to keep the structure as is and just make it more beautiful?" or "Do I need reshaping of my space?" Reviewing portfolios also helps — look for projects that resonate with your style. Speaking to two or three professionals before committing is always worthwhile — the right person will make you feel understood from the very first conversation, and that instinct is usually reliable.

To wrap up, understanding the interior decorator vs designer difference is key to smooth, satisfying home transformations. The right choice depends on your needs, budget, and project complexity.

For more inspiration, visit our resources on home decor trends and discover beautiful wall art at AboutWallArt.com.

Key Takeaways:

  • Interior decorators focus on aesthetics — furniture, wall art, colour, and styling — without structural changes.
  • Interior designers handle structural planning, space layouts, and building regulations alongside aesthetics.
  • Decorators are faster and more affordable; designers take longer but handle complex projects.
  • Match the professional to your project scope to avoid costly misunderstandings.
  • Great wall art is the finishing touch that makes any professionally designed space feel truly personal.

What exactly is japandi style, and why has it captured the imagination of so many UK homeowners? Put simply, it is a design philosophy that merges the clean-lined functionality of Scandinavian interiors with the quiet elegance of Japanese minimalism — producing spaces that feel genuinely restful rather than merely tidy. If you have ever walked into a room and felt an immediate sense of ease without quite knowing why, there is a good chance japandi principles were quietly at work.

By Mae Osz | Interior Design Consultant & Home Decor Expert with 12+ years of experience.

Have you noticed how a decorating trend can completely shift the atmosphere of a room the moment you walk in?

Quick Answer: Japandi style is a design approach that blends Japanese minimalism with Scandinavian functionality to create calm, uncluttered interiors. It relies on a muted, earthy colour palette, natural materials such as wood and linen, and purposeful furniture with clean lines. Carefully chosen wall art in neutral or nature-inspired tones is a key finishing touch that adds warmth without visual noise.

That instant feeling of calm is exactly what the Japandi style is designed to create. Blending Japanese minimalism with Scandinavian functionalism, it’s so much more than just an aesthetic — it’s a way of living with intention.

For many of us in the UK looking to escape the busyness of everyday life, this thoughtful approach has quickly become a favourite decorating trend. Its focus on mindfulness, simplicity, natural materials, and craftsmanship makes it a beautifully refreshing way to design a home.

In this guide, I’ll show you how to bring this serene Japandi look into your own space through art, colour, texture, and mindful styling.

List of Contents

  • The Philosophy Behind a Japandi Home
  • Crafting a Serene Japandi Colour Palette
  • Choosing Furniture with Function and Form
  • Weaving in Natural Textures and Materials
  • Adorning Walls and Floors with Unique Wall Art and Natural Finishes
  • Perfecting the Look with Mindful Accessories
  • Your Simple Checklist for a Balanced Japandi Home

The Rise of Mindful Interiors

The move towards more mindful interiors isn't surprising. We're all looking for ways to make our homes feel like a genuine escape. This is where the Japandi style truly shines. It’s not about chasing a fleeting look but about adopting a mindset that values peace and simplicity.

This particular decorating trend blends the cosy, functional comfort of Scandinavian design with the timeless elegance of Japanese aesthetics.

Think of it as the perfect marriage of 'hygge' (the Danish concept of cosiness) and 'wabi-sabi' (the Japanese appreciation of imperfection). The result is a space that feels both modern and warm, minimal yet inviting. It’s a design philosophy that encourages us to surround ourselves only with things that are beautiful, useful, or both.

This intentional approach is why this decorating trend resonates so deeply with people wanting to create a more balanced life, starting right at home.

Crafting a Serene Japandi Colour Palette

Colour is the foundation of a Japandi home, and getting it right is key to creating that signature sense of calm. I always start with the Scandinavian base: a palette of muted, neutral tones like oatmeal, stone, and soft grey. These colours make a room feel bright, spacious, and instantly relaxing.

Then, to add depth and warmth, I bring in the richer, earthier shades from the Japanese aesthetic. Think of colours like muted greens, terracotta, and charcoal. These prevent the space from feeling too stark or cold. The trick is to create gentle contrast.

For instance, you might paint your walls in a soft off-white and choose a large sofa in a light stone colour. Then, you can introduce a charcoal accent wall or use terracotta and muted green in your cushions, throws, or a statement piece of art. This careful layering of colour is one of the most important calm home decorating ideas.

It’s a decorating trend that proves you don’t need loud colours to make a statement. You can explore how different shades work together by browsing art by colour scheme to find your perfect accents.

Building Your Japandi Colour Scheme

Colour Category Example Colours Where to Use Mood Created
Base Neutrals Oatmeal, Stone, Soft Grey, Off-White Walls, large sofas, flooring Airy, calm, and bright
Earthy Accents Muted Green, Terracotta, Beige Cushions, throws, a single feature wall Warmth, connection to nature
Deep Accents Charcoal, Indigo, Dark Brown Vases, picture frames, small furniture Depth, contrast, and sophistication

This table provides a simple guide for layering colours to achieve the balanced and serene Japandi look. Use it as a starting point to build a palette that feels personal to you.

Choosing Furniture with Function and Form

When it comes to furniture, the Japandi philosophy is beautifully simple: prioritise clean lines, low profiles, and high-quality craftsmanship.

This is a decorating trend that moves away from disposable items and towards pieces that are built to last. Think of iconic shapes like simple platform beds, low-slung sofas, and uncluttered sideboards. Functionality is absolutely essential.

Every piece of furniture should have a clear purpose to help maintain that clutter-free feeling. I love incorporating multifunctional pieces, like a simple wooden bench that can serve as seating in a hallway or as a coffee table in the living room.

A key part of the Japanese Scandinavian design is creating balance by mixing furniture styles. Try pairing the soft, curved shapes of Scandinavian design, like a rounded armchair, with the more angular, refined pieces from Japanese traditions, such as a sleek, rectangular console table.

This is a decorating trend that celebrates thoughtful curation. When selecting pieces from our furniture collection, focus on these materials:

  • Light woods like oak, ash, and maple

  • Sustainable materials like bamboo and rattan

  • Sleek, unadorned frames in black or White

Weaving in Natural Textures and Materials

Texture is what breathes life into a minimalist space, preventing it from feeling cold or one-dimensional. This is where a Japandi style home truly feels warm and inviting. It’s all about engaging the senses with tactile materials. This is my favourite part of this decorating trend because it’s so intuitive. Here are some of the key materials I love to use:

  • Natural Woods: Unfinished or lightly stained woods for furniture, flooring, and decorative objects bring an immediate connection to nature.


Shop Here

  • Woven Fibres: Rattan and bamboo are perfect for adding texture through chairs, decorative screens, and light fixtures.

  • Paper: Delicate paper lampshades, like the famous Akari-style lamps, diffuse light beautifully and add a soft, ethereal quality.
  • Natural Fabrics: Layering different fabrics is essential. I use a mix of linen, cotton, and wool for curtains, cushions, and throws to create a cosy, layered look.

This is also where the Japanese concept of 'wabi-sabi' comes into play. It’s the art of finding beauty in imperfection. Think of handmade ceramics with slight irregularities, a coffee table made from rough-hewn wood, or the natural crinkles in a linen throw.

These details add soul and authenticity, making a space feel lived-in and real. This appreciation for the imperfect is a core element of this unique decorating trend.

Adorning Walls and Floors with the Japandi Decorating trend

In a Japandi home, walls and floors are treated as calm backdrops, not busy canvases. The approach to wall decor is intentionally uncluttered. Instead of a crowded gallery wall, this decorating trend focuses on a single, impactful piece of art that serves as a focal point.

This allows the artwork to truly breathe and make a statement. When looking for prints for your living room, consider art that fits this aesthetic:

  • Abstract pieces with simple, bold lines or organic shapes.

Shop Here

  • Nature-inspired prints, like delicate botanical sketches or serene mountain landscapes.


Shop Here

  • Japanese ink wash (Sumi-e) style paintings that convey a lot with just a few strokes.

Shop Here

I always recommend using simple, natural wood frames to complement the artwork without distracting from it. You can find beautiful examples in our minimalist art collection.

For flooring, light wood, bamboo, or stone-effect tiles work perfectly.

To add softness and define a space, use a simple, low-pile rug made from natural fibres like jute or wool.

This thoughtful approach to minimalist home decor UK creates a wonderful sense of openness and calm. It embraces the philosophy of wabi-sabi, which, as the BBC explains, celebrates the beauty of the imperfect and transient. This mindset is a defining feature of this powerful decorating trend.

Perfecting the Look with Mindful Accessories

The final layer of a Japandi interior is all about mindful accessorising. This is where the 'less is more' philosophy is most apparent.

Every object should be either beautiful or useful, and ideally both. It’s about curating a small collection of meaningful items rather than filling shelves with clutter. Knowing how to create a Japandi interior comes down to these thoughtful final touches.

 This is a decorating trend that values intention over abundance. Here are a few key accessories I always recommend from our decor collection:

  • Bring Nature Indoors: This is one of the easiest and most effective ways to embrace the Japandi style. A simple bonsai tree, a few elegant bamboo stalks, or even a single branch in a beautiful vase can instantly connect your space to the outdoors.


Shop Here

  • Handmade Ceramics: Choose vases, bowls, and mugs with a tangible, handmade quality. Their unique shapes and subtle imperfections add so much character and warmth.


Shop Here

  • Minimalist Lighting: Opt for light fixtures that provide soft, diffused light. Think paper lanterns or simple lamps with fabric shades that create a warm, gentle atmosphere in the evening.

SHOP HERE

  • Simple Trays: An elegant wooden or ceramic tray is perfect for organising small items on a coffee table or sideboard. It groups things together, maintaining that clean, uncluttered look.

Bringing It All Together for a Balanced Space

Creating a cohesive Japandi look is all about finding balance. It’s a delicate dance between light and dark colours, smooth and rough textures, and straight and curved lines. This is the essence of this sophisticated decorating trend.

If you’re just starting, it can feel a bit daunting, but a simple, step-by-step approach makes it manageable. Here’s how I recommend tackling it:

  • Begin with Decluttering: Before you add anything new, create a clean canvas. A tidy space is the cornerstone of Japandi design.
  • Establish the Neutral Palette: Choose your base colours for the walls and large furniture items. This will set the calm tone for the entire room.
  • Choose Key Furniture Pieces: Focus on a few high-quality pieces that prioritise both function and form.
  • Layer in Textures and Mindful Accessories: This is the final step where you add warmth and personality with textiles, plants, and a few cherished objects.

Remember, Japandi is a personal journey, not a rigid set of rules. The goal is to adapt the principles to create a space that genuinely feels restorative to you. 

This is a decorating trend that’s meant to be lived in and loved. Ultimately, this enduring decorating trend is about creating your own personal sanctuary, a calm and balanced Japandi-inspired home that supports your well-being.

Perfecting Your Main Bedroom Decoration with Textiles

A velvet cushion adds a touch of luxury, a chunky knit throw brings rustic charm, and a bouclé chair invites you to curl up with a book.

Don’t forget the floor! A soft rug under the bed not only anchors the space but also feels wonderful underfoot on chilly mornings. This sensory detail is a key part of a successful main bedroom decoration.

The right home decor textiles can completely transform a room, adding colour, pattern, and a sense of luxury. This is where your main bedroom decoration truly comes to life.

Creating Ambience with Thoughtful Lighting

What does the ideal personal retreat actually look like — and how do you make it happen? Man cave decor is no longer about dark walls and a tatty sofa; today it's about crafting a sophisticated, personality-led space that genuinely works for you. Whether you want a cinematic home-cinema setup, a relaxed reading lounge, or a games room with real style, the right design choices can turn even the most uninspiring spare room into somewhere you actually want to spend time.

By Mae Osz | Interior Design Consultant & Home Decor Expert with 12+ years of experience.

Quick Answer: The best man cave decor balances comfort, personal style, and purpose — choose a clear theme, layer your lighting, and invest in one quality anchor piece of furniture. Adding carefully chosen wall art instantly lifts the space and reflects your personality. Keep the palette cohesive, use smart storage to control clutter, and let every element earn its place.

Are you dreaming of a personal space that’s more than just a spare room? It’s a common desire, especially in busy households, to have a corner of the world that is entirely your own.

Let’s explore how thoughtful man cave decor can transform any room into the ultimate sanctuary. This is about creating a space that truly reflects you.

List of Contents

  • In This Guide
  • Defining Your Sanctuary's Purpose
  • Setting the Mood with Colour and Lighting
  • Man Cave Essentials: What Every Space Needs
  • Choosing Furniture That Blends Comfort and Style
  • Personalising Your Space with Unique Wall Art and Accents
  • Man Cave Decor Ideas by Theme

Defining Your Sanctuary’s Purpose

First things first, let's redefine what a 'man cave' can be in 2026. The old clichés are gone. Today, it’s about creating a sophisticated, personal retreat where anyone can unwind. This isn't just a room; it's a personal sanctuary design.

The most important step is deciding its primary purpose. What will you do here?

Will it be a media room for immersive film nights with the family? Perhaps a quiet library for getting lost in a good book? Or maybe it's a high-tech hub for gaming or a refined spot for enjoying music.

This single decision will guide every choice you make, from furniture to lighting and wall art.

For example, a music lover’s retreat might feature acoustic wall panels that double as art, creating both function and beauty.


Shop Here

On the other hand, a reader’s nook would prioritise a supremely comfortable chair and warm, focused lighting.

Thinking about the room's function helps you explore different decor styles and find what truly fits. I see this design process as a form of self-care.

Crafting this space is about embracing small, consistent improvements in your daily life, creating a haven that supports your wellbeing.

Setting the Mood with Colour and Lighting

Now for the fun part: setting the atmosphere. I encourage you to look beyond the stereotypical dark and moody tones. Instead, think about sophisticated and inviting colour palettes that create a specific feeling. Imagine deep navy and warm brass for a classic, club-like feel. Or consider charcoal grey paired with natural wood for a rustic-modern look.

For a truly calming space, consider earthy greens and warm creams. You can find art to match any of these moods by exploring different colour schemes.

Lighting is just as important as colour. I always recommend using layered lighting to create depth and versatility. It’s simpler than it sounds. Think of it in three layers:

  • Ambient Lighting: This is your overall illumination, like a central ceiling fixture or recessed spotlights that light up the whole room.

  • Task Lighting: This is focused light for specific activities. A reading lamp by your favourite chair or under-cabinet lighting at a home bar are perfect examples.

  • Accent Lighting: Use this to highlight the features you love most, like a spotlight on a piece of wall art or LED strips on your shelving.

Smart lighting can also be a wonderful addition, allowing you to change the room's mood with a single tap.

Finally, don't underestimate the power of a statement lighting fixture. A sculptural floor lamp or a set of vintage-style pendant lights can act as a functional centrepiece, adding character and reinforcing the chosen theme of the man cave decor.

Choosing Furniture That Blends Comfort and Style

Integrating Technology Seamlessly

I love clever solutions like smart speakers hidden on bookshelves or a TV that displays artwork when it's off. These touches are central to a modern home decor aesthetic.

Choosing between the many available wall art mediums — canvas, framed prints, metal, wood, or textiles — can feel daunting when every option promises something different. The medium you pick shapes not just how a piece looks, but how it feels in the room: its texture, its weight, and the mood it creates. Understanding each material's strengths makes it far easier to find the right match for your walls, your lighting, and your interior style.

By Mae Osz | Interior Design Consultant & Home Decor Expert with 12+ years of experience.

Quick Answer: The most popular wall art mediums in the UK are canvas, framed prints, metal, wood, and textiles — each suited to different rooms and styles. Canvas and framed prints are the most versatile, working well in living rooms and bedrooms, while metal suits contemporary and office spaces. Choosing the right medium depends on the room's purpose, your interior style, and how much natural light the wall receives.

Have you ever stood in front of a blank wall wondering what type of artwork would bring your room to life? Choosing the right material for your wall art can transform a simple space into a serene retreat. Over the years, I've guided many homeowners through this very dilemma, helping them find their perfect match — whether it's for a cosy living room or a mindful office. But with so many materials available, each with its own character and charm, how do you choose the one that truly fits your home and your mood?

Wall art mediums range from classic canvases to more tactile options like textiles or wood. Each carries different qualities in terms of texture, durability, and style. This variety lets you achieve distinct atmospheres — from calming to energising — depending on your room's purpose. Browse our unique wall art collections for inspiration before you decide.

Key Takeaways

  • Canvas offers warmth and texture — ideal for living rooms and bedrooms where a soft, inviting feel is the goal.
  • Framed prints are the most versatile and durable medium, working beautifully in every room from hallways to offices.
  • Metal art is sleek and modern — best for offices and contemporary spaces, but always balance it with softer textures.
  • Wood panels bring natural warmth and a handcrafted feel — perfect for Scandi, rustic, or transitional interiors.
  • Textile art like macramé or tapestries adds softness, sound absorption, and three-dimensional depth to bedrooms.
  • Mixing mediums — such as a large canvas anchor with framed prints alongside — creates the most layered, curated look.

List of Contents

  • The Best Wall Art Materials for a Calm Bedroom
  • Choosing the Right Art Material for Office and Hallway Spaces
  • How to Size and Position Your Wall Art for Best Effect

What are the Most Popular Materials for Wall Art?

From my experience, when clients first ask about wall art, they're usually considering one or two types — often canvas or framed prints. However, the market has expanded, giving us a rich palette to choose from. The most common wall art mediums I see today include canvas (classic, vivid colours and texture), framed prints (versatile, neat, and protective), metal art (sleek, modern, with great durability), wood art (rustic, warm, with natural texture), and textiles (soft, tactile, and full of depth).

Medium Feel & Texture Durability Style Fit Common Use
Canvas Matte, textured Moderate Contemporary, classic Living room, bedroom
Framed Prints Smooth, polished High Traditional, modern Bedrooms, living rooms, offices
Metal Glossy or matte, cool Very high Industrial, modern Offices, hallways
Wood Warm, tactile High Rustic, Scandi, traditional Living rooms, hallways
Textiles Soft, layered Moderate Boho, Scandi, eclectic Bedrooms, living rooms

How Does Your Choice of Material Affect Room Mood and Style?

Many clients I've worked with underestimate how much the medium alone can change a room's vibe. A vibrant canvas print works wonders in creating a focal point, whilst a wooden panel can subtly warm up the same space without shouting for attention. Canvas offers a tactile feel that instantly adds warmth and dimension. Framed prints protect artwork under glass, making them brilliant for high-traffic spaces. Metal pieces reflect light beautifully and lend a contemporary feel — excellent for striking, minimalist interiors. Wooden wall art adds texture and brings a natural element inside. And textile art like tapestries or macramé adds softness and a three-dimensional effect that can't be achieved with flat prints. Find more inspiration through our unique home decor guides.

Which Materials Work Best for Unique Wall Art in the Living Room?


Shop Here

 

In living rooms, wall art often gets the most attention — and wear. Canvas is a favourite because it offers a balance of softness and vividness. Framed prints, protected by glass, add longevity and a refined appearance. Many clients combine these two — large canvases for focal walls and framed prints for smaller spots. Wood art pieces add an earthy, grounding feel but must be sealed properly to protect against humidity. Choose framed prints with UV-protective glass if near bright windows, avoid placing delicate textiles where children might touch often, and note that metal art suits spaces unlikely to need frequent cleaning. If you want to explore how to arrange multiple pieces once you have chosen your material, our gallery wall layout guide offers room-by-room arrangement ideas to help you plan with confidence.

What Are the Best Wall Art Mediums for Bedroom Decor?

The bedroom should be a calm retreat — a space where you unwind. Textile wall art like tapestries or woven macramé hangings instantly softens a room and absorbs sound, creating a peaceful atmosphere. Canvas art, especially in muted tones, lends a softness that framed glass prints can sometimes lack. And framed prints of calming images or abstract designs work well for a more polished look that's easy to swap when you want to refresh your bedroom decor. For more bedroom art ideas, visit our bedroom decor gallery for pieces that bring serenity into your personal space.

Choosing the Right Art Material for Office and Hallway Spaces


Shop Here

 

Office and hallway walls often get overlooked when considering wall art mediums. Yet the right choice can energise your work mood or set the tone for visitors instantly. Metal art stands up well to office environments — it's durable and visually striking. Framed prints and canvas prints featuring nature or abstract designs create visual depth in hallways. It's a personal favourite to mix mediums here for a gallery effect. To see some options that work well in these spaces, explore our office decor and hallway decor collections. You can also find wall art styling inspiration across our full range.

How to Size and Position Your Wall Art for Best Effect

Once you have chosen your medium, getting the size and placement right is what separates a room that looks considered from one that looks unfinished. As a general rule, a single piece of artwork should cover roughly two-thirds of the wall width above a sofa or console — this applies whether you choose a large canvas or a framed print.

Hang artwork so that its centre sits at approximately eye level, which in most UK homes means around 145–150 cm from the floor. If you are grouping pieces into a gallery wall, keep the gaps between frames consistent at 5–8 cm for a cohesive look. For hallways, where wall space is narrow, tall vertical pieces or a simple two-column arrangement tend to work far better than a wide horizontal layout.

Before putting a nail in the wall, cut paper templates to the exact dimensions of each piece and use masking tape to mock up the arrangement — this saves time and avoids unnecessary holes. If you are unsure where to start, our gallery wall layout guide walks through room-by-room arrangements in detail.

To wrap up, the choice of wall art mediums shapes not only your decor but also the feel of your home. Whether you lean towards the warmth of wood, the softness of textiles, the vibrancy of canvas, or the sleekness of metal, it's all about matching the medium to your personal style and space needs. Don't shy away from mixing mediums to create layers and harmony — the perfect combination can make your walls speak your aesthetic language without saying a word.

Wondering how to make a rented flat or house actually feel like home? Rental décor is the art of adding personality, warmth, and style to a space you don't own — without leaving a mark the landlord can bill you for. The good news is that damage-free decorating has come a long way, and there are more clever options than ever to transform bare white walls and bland floors into a space that genuinely reflects who you are.

By Mae Osz | Interior Design Consultant & Home Decor Expert with 12+ years of experience.

Rentals can be rigid, sure. Rental Decor is not easy. White walls that seem to repel character, flooring that whispers “don’t scratch me,” and rules stacked as high as the moving boxes you haven’t unpacked. But limitations aren’t death sentences. They’re blueprints for creative rebellion. With a few clever decisions, a pinch of style, and a bit of strategy, you can turn a rental into a space that feels unmistakably yours. No landlords harmed in the making. 

Quick Answer: The best rental décor uses damage-free methods — peel-and-stick wallpaper, command hooks, leaned or removable wall art, layered rugs, and flexible lighting — to add personality without voiding your tenancy agreement. Focus on textiles, lighting, and statement wall art to create the biggest visual impact without touching the structure. You can completely transform a rented room without a single nail or landlord conversation.

List of Contents

  • Work With What the Kitchen Gave You
  • Make Your Home Office Flow
  • Reclaim the Bedroom
  • Transform Blank Walls With Unique Wall Art and Removable Décor

Start Where Guests Start

The entryway and living room set the tone, so don’t let them scream “temporary.” Rethink your lighting, rugs, and especially your furniture finishes. A cohesive look with consistent finishes—like all wood tones or all black accents—can unify mismatched pieces instantly. Layer in peel-and-stick hooks for hanging coats, keys, and the occasional rogue umbrella. Add a mirror to fake more square footage and bounce light around the room. You’ve just redefined the vibe without driving a nail into the wall.


Shop Here

Work With What the Kitchen Gave You

Rental kitchens often come with odd layouts, little counter space, and zero charm. Accept it, then outsmart it. Use vertical space wherever you can—maximise kitchen storage with pegboards or racks that can hang without drilling. Swap in nicer drawer pulls and cabinet knobs, then stash the originals to reinstall later. Throw down a machine-washable rug to soften the space and catch whatever breakfast throws at it. And if your landlord didn’t leave enough light, that’s what puck lights are for.

Make Your Home Office Flow

If you’re working from a corner desk squeezed between your bed and a laundry basket, it’s time for a reset. Feng shui might sound abstract, but its many benefits can be surprisingly practical. Position your desk so you face the door or most of the room, not a wall. This gives you psychological command and cuts that boxed-in vibe. Add a plant—not a fake one—something green and thriving that signals energy and growth. Keep cords tidy and hide your modem like it’s an ex you’d rather forget.


Shop Here

Reclaim the Bedroom

Bedrooms in rentals are notoriously underwhelming, but they don’t have to be. Think in layers—soft lighting, textured bedding, and curtains that puddle slightly on the floor. Swap out your nightstand for something with drawers and ditch anything too bulky. A storage ottoman has hidden space for linens or the clothes you swore you'd fold last week. Use command hooks to hang art or photos at eye level and avoid that “everything's floating too high” look. If you want personality without permanence, try fabric headboards that you can attach with Velcro.


Shop Here

Dress the Walls, Change the Mood

Bare walls feel like a waiting room, not a home. Art changes that fast—it pulls focus, adds emotion, and fills the quiet. You don’t need an art degree or a gallery budget to make it work, just a sense of what makes you pause. Start with one big piece or a series that speaks to you, then build around it slowly. For thoughtfully curated, striking prints that transform blank space into something bold, explore the selections at About Wall Art.

Bring Light Back In

Most rentals light your space like an airport terminal. You’re going to fix that. Replace the harsh overheads with floor lamps or table lamps that give off a warm, golden hue. Invest in battery-powered LED strips or wireless, easy-to-install options with sticky backing for closets and kitchen corners. No electrician required. Swap out boring shades for fabric ones that cast softer light. Even fairy lights can work, as long as you don’t drape them like a dorm room disaster. Think glow, not glare.

Let the Walls Talk Back

White walls are just empty conversation. Speak up. Peel-and-stick decor is your loophole to colour, texture, and everything in between. Try one wall with removable peel & stick wallpaper or decals that don’t look like they belong in a kid’s room. Lean large framed art instead of hanging it, especially if you’re short on command strips. Create a gallery wall using washi tape or magnetic frames. Shelving units that rest on the floor but give the illusion of floating can also trick the eye and hold your treasures.

No rental comes pre-loaded with your taste, but that’s not the point. You don’t need gut renovations or permission slips to create a space that feels right. What you need is intention, adaptability, and maybe a little rebellion. Move furniture until the room works better, then add colour where it doesn’t “belong.” Use rules as a ceiling, not a blueprint. And remember, personality never needed a security deposit.

What does it really take to create a family room that looks great and holds up to everyday life? The answer lies in a handful of stylish practical decorating tips that prioritise both aesthetics and function — no compromise required. From choosing the right fabrics to planning a layout that flows, the decisions you make early on shape how much you'll love the space for years to come. In this guide, we'll walk through every key area so you can create a family room that feels as good as it looks.

By Mae Osz | Interior Design Consultant & Home Decor Expert with 12+ years of experience.

Looking for decorating tips for family room that’s both stylish and comfortable? You’re not alone. The family room is the true heart of the home—a place for laughter, relaxation, and cherished memories. Yet, keeping it beautiful amid the joyful chaos of everyday life, from children’s toys to pet-friendly needs, can feel like a real challenge.

Quick Answer: The most effective approach to family room decorating is to layer comfort and style — start with durable, family-friendly furniture in warm neutral tones, then build character through textures, lighting, and personalised wall art. Focus on a flexible layout that suits how your family actually uses the space, and choose pieces that are easy to clean without sacrificing good looks.

That’s why I want to share some practical decorating tips for a family room that feels both chic and completely liveable. Creating this kind of sanctuary doesn’t mean sacrificing your personal style—it’s all about making smart, thoughtful choices. Together, we’ll explore how to infuse the space with your family’s unique personality, transforming it into a room everyone loves to be in.

Choosing Comfortable and Durable Furniture

The furniture you choose forms the foundation of your family room, so it needs to be both beautiful and ready for anything. These foundational decorating tips for family room are about choosing wisely for the long term, ensuring your space remains a family friendly living room design for years to come.

The Sofa: Your Room's Anchor

I always say the sofa is the main event. When selecting one, think about fabrics that are both stylish and tough. Performance velvets offer a luxe look with surprising resilience, while tightly woven cottons provide a casual feel. My personal favourite for busy homes is leather that develops a beautiful patina over time. And here’s a game-changing tip: look for sofas with removable, washable covers. They are an absolute lifesaver.

Beyond the Sofa: Accent Seating

While the sofa is key, don’t forget accent seating. Mixing in a couple of comfortable armchairs adds so much personality and provides flexible seating options when you have guests. It breaks up the monotony of a matching suite and allows you to play with different shapes and fabrics.

Smart Tables for Modern Families

When it comes to coffee and side tables, safety and storage are paramount. I always recommend tables with rounded edges, especially with little ones running around. Many modern designs also come with built-in storage, which is perfect for hiding away remote controls, magazines, and other clutter. Investing in quality construction is another of my non-negotiable decorating tips for family room; a sturdy frame will withstand daily life beautifully.

Weaving in Warm Colour Schemes and Textures

Colour and texture are what create the emotional atmosphere of a room. I always suggest starting with a base of warm neutrals like greige, mushroom, or a soft terracotta. These shades are wonderfully inviting and are also quite forgiving with the scuffs and marks of daily life. From there, you can introduce layers to add depth and cosiness. This is one of the most impactful decorating tips for family room you can use. It’s all about creating a sensory experience that feels comforting and complete, which is central to any cosy family room ideas UK.

Here’s how I love to layer textures for a rich, inviting feel:

  • Underfoot: A plush wool or high-pile rug instantly softens the space and helps to define the main seating area.
  • On the Sofa: Mix and match cushions in different materials. Think velvet, linen, and bouclé to create visual interest and tactile comfort.

For Warmth:

  • Nothing says cosy like a chunky knit or faux fur throw blanket draped over an armchair, ready for snuggling.
  • For Storage: Woven baskets are my go-to for stylishly stashing magazines, toys, or extra blankets.

If you want to introduce bolder colours without overwhelming the room, consider an accent wall or a piece of statement wall art. A large abstract canvas can beautifully tie together all the accent colours you've chosen. In fact, you can explore our collections to find art that perfectly matches your vision by browsing our gallery wall art by colour scheme. These are simple yet effective decorating tips for a family room that make a huge impact.

Functional Layout and Space Planning Tips

A well-thought-out layout is one of the most transformative decorating tips for family room. It’s all about making the room work for you and your family’s daily life. Knowing how to arrange family room furniture properly can make the difference between a cluttered room and a harmonious one.

Creating Conversational Zones

Here’s a simple change that encourages connection: arrange your sofas and chairs to face each other, rather than all pointing towards the television. This naturally creates a conversational zone, making it easier for family members to interact and spend quality time together.

Ensuring Smooth Traffic Flow

It’s vital to leave clear pathways for people to move around easily. A practical tip is to use a large rug to anchor the main seating area. Then, ensure there is enough space to walk around it without bumping into furniture. This creates a sense of order and makes the room feel more spacious and less chaotic.

The Power of Multi-Functional Pieces

In a family room, every piece of furniture should work hard. I’m a huge fan of pieces that do double duty. Think of an ottoman that opens up for storage, a nest of tables that can be separated and moved where needed, or a console table behind the sofa that can act as a serving area or a temporary desk. For those with open-plan homes, you can use the back of a sofa or a tall bookshelf to create a subtle visual division between the living area and a dining space. These smart decorating tips for family room maximise every square inch.

Personalised Decor and Wall Art

This is where your family's unique story truly comes to life. The most meaningful decorating tips for family room are those that help you infuse the space with personality. I always encourage clients to choose decor that is genuinely special to them. A fantastic way to do this is by creating a gallery wall. Try mixing cherished family photos in cohesive frames with your children's favourite artwork and prints that evoke happy memories. My tip for arranging them is to start with a central piece and build outwards for a balanced, organic look.


Shop Here

Another powerful element is statement wall art for living room UK. A single, large-scale canvas painting or a triptych can serve as the room's stunning centrepiece, anchoring the entire design and colour palette. It’s a simple way to achieve a high-impact, stylish living room decor. These personal decorating tips for a family room are what turn a house into a home. You can also add other personal touches, like displaying travel souvenirs on floating shelves or dedicating a bookshelf to favourite family reads. When choosing art, our collection of framed wall pictures for the living room offers a wide variety of styles to suit any personality and help you tell your story.

Creating Ambience with Layered Lighting

Lighting is one of those things that can completely change the feel of a space, yet it's often overlooked. Implementing clever lighting is one of my favourite decorating tips for family room because it makes a huge difference in how the space feels. The secret is layering your light sources. I break it down into three simple types:

  1. Ambient Lighting: This is your overall light, usually from a central ceiling fixture or recessed downlights. It provides the base level of illumination for the room.
  2. Task Lighting: This is more focused light for specific activities. Think of a floor lamp by an armchair for reading or a desk lamp on a console table.
  3. Accent Lighting: This is gentle light used to highlight features you love, such as a picture light over a favourite piece of art or uplighting for a houseplant.

Warmth and control are everything. I always advise using bulbs with a warm white glow (around 2700K) and installing dimmer switches wherever possible. This allows you to shift the mood from bright and energetic for playtime to soft and cosy for a family film night. Finally, don’t forget the power of natural light! Use light, airy curtains or blinds that can be fully opened to make the room feel larger and more cheerful during the day. These simple decorating tips for family room will create an atmosphere everyone loves.

A Space for Everyone to Love

Creating a family room that is both stylish and comfortable is entirely achievable with a bit of thoughtful planning. I hope these ideas have shown you that you don’t have to choose between a beautiful space and a practical one. By focusing on the key pillars we've discussed—choosing durable furniture, layering warm colours and textures, planning a functional layout, adding personal touches, and using layered lighting—you can design a room that truly works for everyone. The most effective decorating tips for family room are those that help you create a space that not only looks good but also serves your family's needs and brings you joy every single day. Why Eco-Friendly Materials Matter in Interior Design

Eco-conscious decor materials refers to resources used in home decor that reduce environmental impact whilst promoting health and durability. These include reclaimed wood, natural fibres like jute and linen, recycled glass or metal, and paints with low or zero volatile organic compounds (VOCs). Many clients I've worked with initially view sustainable materials as niche or difficult to source — but through my experience, I've often recommended these materials to solve multiple decorating challenges at once.

They enhance air quality, supporting wellbeing. Their natural textures and colours create calming atmospheres. And they avoid fast-fashion decor mistakes — sustainable items tend to offer timeless style that doesn't date. One common mistake I often see with homeowners is opting for cheap mass-produced pieces without regard for material origin. These can quickly lose their charm and wear poorly. In contrast, these eco-friendly materials offer longevity plus a story — often a conversation starter in your home. For those interested in the why and how, our guide to home interior design in five steps walks through broader design principles that work beautifully alongside eco-conscious material choices.

How to Use Reclaimed Wood in Your Home

How to Verify Sustainability Claims When Buying Materials

With so many products marketed as 'natural' or 'eco-friendly', knowing what to look for on a label is genuinely useful. Greenwashing is common in the home decor market, so a little due diligence at the point of purchase goes a long way.

Bringing sustainable interior design materials into your home is a rewarding approach that promotes wellbeing, reduces environmental impact, and creates truly calming interiors. Whether you're starting with reclaimed wood, exploring natural fibre textiles, switching to low-VOC paints, or incorporating recycled finishes, each choice helps create a space that feels both beautiful and responsible. Have you ever stood in your bathroom and wondered what to do with that awkward blank wall just above the toilet? It's a small space frequently overlooked but packed with potential. Whether your bathroom is tiny or spacious, that area can transform from neglected to eye-catching with a touch of creativity and the right above toilet decor.

Bathrooms often serve as personal spaces where mindful design and calming aesthetics enhance daily routines. Creative Ways to Display Wall Art Above the Toilet

Above toilet decor is an excellent opportunity to personalise and bring functionality to this compact area. Instead of leaving the wall bare, consider creative ways to enhance it. Here are some inspirational ideas to get you started:

Floating Shelves for Display and Storage

Installing floating shelves is a classic move. They add storage without feeling bulky, ideal for placing candles, small plants, or elegant bathroom accessories. For a more considered look, choose shelves in natural wood tones or keep them sleek and white to maintain a Scandinavian vibe. The beauty of floating shelves is that they can be styled differently over time as your taste evolves, without any structural commitment.

Basket Accents to Add Texture

Woven baskets or rattan trays add warmth and offer a place to keep extra toilet paper, toiletries, or dried flowers. Using baskets cleverly blends storage and decor, preventing bathroom clutter. Art and Prints for Personality

Sometimes a single piece of artwork can become a conversation starter and transform the above toilet area entirely. Consider calming nature prints or abstract designs that evoke mindfulness, complementing your overall bathroom aesthetic.

Browse our unique wall art collection for pieces that work beautifully in bathroom spaces — and if you're refreshing the whole room, our guide to decorating a powder room with style covers fixtures, colour palettes, and finishing touches from start to finish.

Mixed Materials for Interest

  • Incorporate metal, wood, and glass elements.
  • Mix framed art alongside floating shelves and baskets.
  • This combination adds depth and balance to your bathroom's personality.

These ideas can be tailored to your bathroom's size and style, ensuring the finished look harmonises with your existing decor collection effortlessly.

How to Choose the Right Art for Above the Toilet

Artwork above the toilet not only adds visual appeal but also personal touches that bring a bathroom to life. However, selecting the right size and style is key to preventing overpowering the space or looking too sparse. The right piece in the right position can make a small bathroom feel intentional and considered rather than simply functional.

Understanding the Space

First, measure how much wall space is available. Generally, since the area can be narrow, choosing pieces that work well within a vertical space ensures flow and balance. Avoid artwork that's wider than the toilet or too small to be noticed. A good rule of thumb is to keep the art width within 75% of the toilet's width for a proportional, grounded look.

Artwork Size Recommended Usage Approximate Wall Space Covered

Choosing the Style

For a calming bathroom atmosphere, consider botanical prints, minimalist black and white photography, or abstract watercolour art. The goal is to choose pieces that complement your bathroom's colour palette whilst introducing a unique character. Artwork that references nature — leaves, botanicals, water — tends to feel particularly at home in a bathroom setting and never looks out of place as the rest of the room evolves.

Artwork above the toilet can become the highlight of your bathroom, especially when paired with coordinated bathroom decor options. Thoughtful selection enhances aesthetic expression without overcrowding the walls.

Balancing Storage and Style on Your Toilet Wall

Adding storage above the toilet is advantageous, especially in compact bathrooms. However, balancing storage with a stylish look is critical to avoid clutter and maintain the calming atmosphere you want. The key is to treat every item on display as a deliberate choice rather than a default — if it doesn't serve a purpose or add something visually, it probably doesn't need to be there.

Layered Storage Systems

Layer shelves with baskets and decorative items. This approach divides storage visually to maintain neatness whilst keeping frequently used items handy. For instance, place toiletries in baskets on the lower shelf and display attractive decor pieces like framed art on the top. The layered approach also makes it easy to refresh the look seasonally without changing the structure.

Choose Style-Friendly Storage Solutions

  • Opt for storage solutions like sleek floating shelves or built-in cubbies that match bathroom textures.
  • Use neutral tones to maintain harmony or glass shelving to keep the area light and open.

Keep Essentials Organised

Use containers or boxes for small items to avoid a messy surface. Remember, the goal is to add storage without making the space feel cramped. Decanting everyday items into matching containers — even simple white ceramic pots — instantly elevates the look and makes the shelf feel curated rather than utilitarian.

Combining storage and style this way complements your existing unique home decor, making everyday essentials accessible yet beautifully organised.

What are the best above toilet decor ideas for small bathrooms?

Small bathrooms pose decorating challenges, but the space above your toilet offers a prime opportunity to add both style and function without overcrowding. Here are my favourite above toilet decor ideas for small bathrooms

If the toilet is part of a compact en suite or cloakroom, the same principles of vertical thinking and careful proportion apply throughout — our round-up of small restroom decor ideas covers clever storage, lighting, and layout tips for the tightest spaces.

Slim Floating Shelves

Choose narrow floating shelves that won't protrude too much. These provide room for essentials like scented candles, small potted plants, or a few decorative items without taking up space. Keeping the shelf depth under 20cm ensures it stays proportional to the toilet below and doesn't feel imposing.

Mirrors to Reflect Light

Adding a small, stylish mirror above the toilet can open up the space visually. Circular or uniquely shaped mirrors add charm and make your bathroom feel bigger. They also bounce natural light around the room, which is particularly valuable in bathrooms without windows.

Vertical Storage Units

If you want more storage, consider vertical wall-mounted shelving units. They're slim but maximise the vertical space efficiently. Going vertical rather than horizontal is the single most effective strategy for adding storage in a small bathroom without making it feel smaller.

Wall-Mounted Baskets

Utilise woven baskets attached to the wall for holding extra toilet rolls or small linens. They add texture without weight. A pair of matching baskets at different heights creates a simple, considered arrangement that feels intentional rather than improvised.

Minimal Clean Lines

Keep decoration minimal and consistent with your bathroom style. Avoid clutter by selecting fewer, meaningful pieces that complement the room's aesthetic. In a small bathroom, every item is visible from every angle — so each piece needs to earn its place.

How do you decorate above the toilet without drilling holes?

Many renters or those who prefer not to damage walls often ask, "How do you decorate above the toilet without drilling holes?" Fortunately, there are several practical options to beautify this space without permanent fixtures. The no-drill approach has improved enormously in recent years — modern adhesive products are strong enough to hold shelves, frames, and hooks securely in bathroom conditions.

Adhesive Shelves and Hooks

Modern adhesive shelves use strong, damage-free glue strips that can hold lightweight items such as plants, candles, or small storage containers. The key is selecting products designed for bathroom humidity and weight limits. Always check the maximum load rating before hanging anything heavier than a small plant or candle.

Tension Rod Shelving

A tension rod setup between walls above the toilet can support hanging baskets or lightweight shelves. This method requires no drilling and can be easily removed. It works particularly well in alcove bathrooms where the walls are close enough to create a stable tension fit.

Wall Decals and Temporary Art

To add personality without frames, use waterproof wall decals or removable sticky hooks for hanging lightweight prints or fabric art. Many removable decals are now designed specifically for humid environments and peel away cleanly without leaving residue.

Lean and Layer

Place leaning art or decorative trays on the toilet tank or slim cabinets nearby. This doesn't use the wall space but keeps the above area visually tidy. A small framed print leaning against the wall on a tank-top tray can look just as considered as a hung piece, with none of the commitment.

These no-drill methods allow you to personalise your space whilst respecting rental agreements and avoiding hassle.

What size artwork looks best for above toilet decor?

Picking the right artwork size is essential to create a well-balanced feature above your toilet. Generally, a piece that's too large overwhelms the space, whilst something too small will get lost. The goal is a piece that feels purposeful — clearly chosen for that spot rather than placed there by default.

Ideal Dimensions

Medium artworks around 40cm by 60cm are typically ideal. They align visually with the width of the toilet and fill the vertical space nicely without dominating the entire wall. If your ceiling is particularly high, a slightly taller piece or a stacked pair of prints can help fill the space without going too wide.

Gallery Walls or Groupings

If a single art piece feels too bold, combine several smaller framed prints (around 30cm square) grouped together. This arrangement adds interest without overpowering your bathroom. Treat the group as a single shape when planning the layout — the overall arrangement should sit within the same proportional guidelines as a single medium piece.

Spacing and Placement Tips

  • Leave a 15–20cm gap between the toilet tank and bottom of the artwork.
  • Keep the artwork centred horizontally above the toilet.

How can you add storage above the toilet without cluttering the bathroom?

Add storage to your bathroom wisely, avoiding a cluttered look above the toilet. Achieving this balance requires strategic placement and selection of storage items. The most effective approach is to decide upfront how many items will live on each shelf and stick to it — creep is the enemy of a calm bathroom.

Use Baskets and Containers

Keep essentials organised inside baskets or storage boxes. These hide clutter yet create a tidy appearance, especially when colour-coordinated or matching bathroom textures. Matching containers — even simple ones — immediately make a shelf look more intentional and less like a dumping ground.

Limit the Number of Items

Display only frequently used or decorative items above the toilet. Store less-used toiletries elsewhere to keep the space from feeling overcrowded. A good rule is no more than five items per shelf — fewer if the shelf is narrow.

Opt for Open and Closed Storage

  • Use shelves combined with covered baskets or boxes.
  • Closed storage hides clutter but open shelves add visual interest.

Incorporate Style-Focused Storage

Choose storage that feels like decor — for example, woven baskets or stylish ceramic containers — which add personality and softness to the bathroom setting. When storage looks beautiful in its own right, the line between function and decoration disappears entirely, which is exactly the effect you're aiming for.

Common Mistakes to Avoid When Decorating Above the Toilet

One of the most useful things the DIY Playbook's widely read bathroom article highlights is that decorating above the toilet is less about what you add and more about what you avoid. Knowing the pitfalls saves you from reworking the space twice.

Hanging art too high. The most common error is fixing a piece so high it floats away from the toilet visually. The centre of any artwork or shelf arrangement should sit roughly 15–20 cm above the cistern lid, keeping everything connected to the fixture rather than hovering on an unrelated patch of wall.

Going too wide. Artwork or shelving that extends beyond the width of the toilet looks unbalanced. Aim for a total width no greater than the toilet's footprint — usually 40–60 cm — so the arrangement feels proportional.

Overcrowding the space. More items do not mean more style. Two or three well-chosen pieces — a shelf, a small print, and a trailing plant — create a curated look. Any more than that tips into clutter and actually makes a bathroom feel smaller.

Ignoring the humidity. Standard paper prints and untreated wood can warp or discolour in a steamy bathroom. Choose moisture-resistant frames, sealed prints, or materials designed for damp environments. Browse our bathroom wall art collection for prints produced on humidity-resistant stock.

Bathroom Aesthetic Guides: Styling Unique Wall Art Above the Toilet

The space above the toilet should feel like a natural extension of your bathroom's overall aesthetic rather than an afterthought. Here is how to tailor the look to the most popular interior styles.

Scandi and minimalist: A single oversized botanical print in a slim white frame, paired with one narrow floating shelf holding a small ceramic pot. Restrict the palette to black, white, and natural timber.

Coastal and relaxed: Soft watercolour seascape prints work beautifully here. Pair with a woven rattan shelf and a small driftwood-style hook for a relaxed, holiday feel without being literal about it.

Japandi: Asymmetric arrangements suit this style well — consider one tall, narrow print alongside a small handmade ceramic vessel on a thin shelf. Earthy neutrals and negative space are the key.

Maximalist or eclectic: A small gallery wall of three to four mixed frames — different sizes but a cohesive colour palette — adds personality without overwhelming the space. Keep frame finishes consistent (all black or all brass) to stop it feeling chaotic.

Classic and traditional: A single framed mirror above the cistern with a small carved shelf below works well. Choose aged gold or antique bronze hardware to complement traditional fittings.

Bathroom Art Dos and Don'ts: What Actually Works Above the Toilet

Knowing what to avoid is just as useful as knowing what looks good. The wall above the toilet has specific constraints — humidity, narrow width, proximity to the cistern — that rule out certain choices before you even begin.

Do choose frames with sealed or lacquered finishes, which resist condensation far better than raw wood or metal that can rust or warp over time. A bathroom generates more moisture than almost any other room, so material choice genuinely matters here.

Do opt for prints under glass or high-quality giclée prints on moisture-resistant stock. Canvas can work if the bathroom is well ventilated, but paper-based prints need glazing to survive long-term in a steamy environment.

Don't hang oversized artwork that extends beyond the toilet's footprint — it immediately looks off-balance and can make a small bathroom feel cluttered rather than considered.

Don't use too many small pieces that compete for attention. A gallery wall can work above the toilet, but it needs a tight, intentional grid rather than a loose scatter. When in doubt, one well-chosen print beats five mismatched ones.

If you're browsing options, our bathroom wall art collection includes prints specifically selected for humid environments, with frame options suited to this space.

Key Takeaways:

  • The wall above your toilet is prime real estate — floating shelves, artwork, and baskets can transform it from blank to beautiful.
  • Medium artworks (40x60cm) are the ideal size for bathroom above toilet decor in most spaces.
  • Balance storage and style by layering baskets with decorative items — function doesn't have to mean clutter.
  • No-drill options like adhesive shelves and removable hooks make this accessible for renters too.
  • Keep small bathrooms feeling open by choosing slim shelves, minimal pieces, and light-reflecting mirrors.

That blank wall above the bed is one of the most valuable — and most overlooked — spaces in any master bedroom. The right master bedroom wall art above bed can anchor the entire room, drawing the eye upward and pulling together colour, texture, and mood in a single well-chosen piece. But knowing where to begin — what size, what style, how high to hang it — is where most people get stuck. This guide walks you through every decision, step by step. 

By Mae Osz | Interior Design Consultant & Home Decor Expert with 12+ years of experience.

Have you ever stood back to admire your master bedroom, only to feel like something's missing above the bed? That blank space often gets overlooked, yet it's a golden opportunity to express your style and create a calm, inviting sanctuary. Choosing the right artwork above your bed could transform your space into a soothing retreat or an inspiring spot to start your day.

Quick Answer: For a master bedroom, choose wall art that spans roughly 60–75% of the bed's width and hang it 20–25 cm above the headboard. Opt for calming subjects — landscapes, botanicals, or soft abstract pieces — in tones that complement your existing bedroom palette. A single large-format print or a neatly arranged gallery of two or three pieces works best in this space.

Wall art above the bed is not just a decorative afterthought—it's the heart of your bedroom's personality. Whether your style leans towards minimalistic, classic, or contemporary, the right artwork brings harmony and balance to your master bedroom. It sets the mood, draws the eye, and makes your bedroom feel truly yours. But how do you pick the perfect piece, decide on the right size, or determine how high to hang it? Let's explore those questions and guide you to creating a stunning focal point that complements your master bedroom style.

Explore practical hints on scale, placement, colour, and framing to create that cohesive, calming atmosphere you're after.

Creating the Perfect Above-Bed Focal Point in Your Master Bedroom

When it comes to decorating above the bed, starting with the right piece is key. The artwork above your bed should create a peaceful environment while also reflecting your personality. Think of it as the centrepiece that invites relaxation and mindfulness. You want something that complements the existing decor without overwhelming it.

Consider first the mood you want to instil. Soft, nature-inspired themes like landscapes or botanical prints work wonderfully for calming a bedroom. Alternatively, abstract art with muted colours can express a modern, artistic vibe without demanding too much attention. For a classic look, framed photographic prints or vintage-style paintings can add an element of timelessness.

Tip: If your room has a neutral palette, pick wall art with a pop of colour to bring warmth without sacrificing calm. Conversely, if your bedroom colour scheme is vibrant, opt for more subtle artwork to balance the space.

Remember, your master bedroom is a retreat. The right piece of bedroom wall art should gently draw you in every day.


Shop Now

Planning Scale and Placement for Bedroom Wall Art Above the Bed

The size and placement of wall art above your bed can make or break the overall effect. Get these wrong, and your artwork might look awkward or even clash with the bed itself.

What Size Wall Art Works Best?

The golden rule for wall art above a bed is to aim for a scale between 60–75% of the bed width. This lets the artwork feel balanced without overpowering the space or disappearing into it. For a typical UK double bed (around 135 cm wide), consider wall art roughly 80 to 100 cm wide.

If you prefer multiple pieces, try creating a gallery wall with smaller artworks arranged cohesively. Just keep the combined width within that 60–75% range.

Where to Hang Your Artwork?

Height is equally essential. Generally, aim for the bottom of the artwork to sit about 20 to 25 cm above the headboard. This creates a natural visual flow and prevents the art from feeling cramped or disconnected.

For very tall ceilings, you could hang it slightly higher but avoid going above eye level when sitting on the bed. You want to engage with the art comfortably.

Choosing Colours and Frames to Enhance Your Bedroom Wall Art

Colour Palette Considerations

  • Soothing neautrals: Soft whites, greys, and earthy tones compliment most bedrooms and keep the mood calm.
  • Accent colours: Blues, greens, or muted pinks can evoke calmness and relaxation, excellent for bedrooms seeking mindfulness.
  • Bold contrasts: If your room has subdued walls and furniture, a piece with contrasting colours can add vibrancy and style.

Remember, whatever colours you choose, they should flow naturally with your bedding, curtains, and other accessories. For some great complementary choices, check out our interior design concepts.

Selecting the Right Frame

Frames do more than just hold your art—they can amplify the style of the whole room. Here are some tips to help:

  • Light wood frames bring warmth and align wonderfully with Scandinavian or natural themes.
  • Black metal frames introduce a modern, sleek look perfect for minimalist interiors.
  • Classic ornate frames add a touch of elegance and work well with traditional or vintage decor.
  • Frameless canvases create a clean, contemporary vibe and allow colours to take centre stage.

Key insight: Match your frame finish to other furniture hardware, such as bedside lamps or drawers, for a harmonious feel.

Abstract Art

Abstract pieces encourage imagination while providing soothing colours or dynamic forms. Look for ones with muted palettes for relaxation, or soft brush strokes that feel fluid.

Landscape and Nature Prints

These bring the outdoors in, promoting mindfulness through scenic views—beach sunrises, forest trails, or gentle water reflections.

Botanical Art

From detailed leaf prints to delicate florals, botanical pieces introduce organic texture. They suit every style from mid-century modern to rustic.

Black & White Photography

A classic choice that adds sophistication without overwhelming with colour. Consider serene cityscapes, delicate architecture, or calming portraits.

Minimalist Line Art

Sleek and modern, line art creates subtle interest. Often monochrome, it enhances a tranquil setting and pairs well with light frames.

Above-Bed Art Ideas for Every Bedroom Decor Style

  • Scandinavian style: Opt for minimalist abstract art or soft botanicals. Keep it simple with clean frames and neutral tones.
  • Modern farmhouse: Rustic landscapes or vintage typography prints work beautifully above a wooden bedframe.

How do you choose the right art for above the bed?

Choosing master bedroom wall art above bed involves a blend of personal taste, room design, and practical dimensions. First, reflect on your bedroom's existing style and colour palette. What feelings do you want to evoke? Peacefulness, energy, or maybe understated elegance?

Then, consider the wall space—not just the width and height but how the art relates to the bed's headboard. If your bed is simple, a bold piece adds interest. If your headboard is ornate, choose something subtler to avoid visual competing.

Don't rush. Use proofs, templates, or temporary placements when possible. Lighting also affects how your art looks; check your chosen piece in different daylight and artificial light conditions.

Remember: the best master bedroom wall art above bed is one that you love waking up to and coming home to, day after day.

What size wall art should go above a master bed?

Choosing the size for your master bedroom wall art above bed is about scale and balance. Aim for artwork that measures 60–75% of the width of your bed to create a balanced look. For example:

  • King Bed (150 cm wide): wall art width should be 90 to 113 cm
  • Super King Bed (180 cm wide): wall art width should be 108 to 135 cm

If you're going for multiple artworks, consider the total combined width with spacing kept minimal and consistent. This method provides more creative freedom, but the overall art "group" should still fit within the 60–75% width of your bed.

Too small a piece looks lost; too large can feel overwhelming and cluttered. Use the infographic below to help visualise the perfect sizes for your bed.

How high should wall art hang above the bed?

The ideal height for master bedroom wall art above bed is roughly 20 to 25 cm above the headboard. This distance creates a natural connection between the bed and the artwork, without feeling cramped or broken.

If your bed has a low-profile headboard or no headboard at all, you might allow a little extra space up to 30 cm, but aim not to exceed eye level when sitting up in bed.

Hanging the art too high can disconnect it from the rest of your bedroom focal point, while too low can feel cluttered. A good rule is to get comfortable sitting upright and glance where the artwork sits in your line of sight.

What styles of wall art work best above a master bedroom bed?

Styles that work best for master bedroom wall art above bed tend to evoke calmness and harmony, although your taste plays the ultimate role. Here are some popular styles:

What to Consider Before You Buy: A Quick Checklist

Bed width: Measure your bed frame and aim for artwork that covers 60–75% of that width.

Ceiling height: Taller ceilings can accommodate larger or taller pieces without feeling oppressive.

Existing palette: Note your wall colour, bedding tones, and furniture finishes before choosing hues.

Lighting: Consider whether the artwork will be naturally lit or whether you need a picture light or uplighter to show it off properly.

Single piece vs. gallery: Decide early — a single oversized print is bold and simple to hang, while a gallery wall offers flexibility but requires more planning.

Final Thoughts: Creating a Bedroom You Love
